# BOOK 1 of 2: THE YOUNG NAVAL CAPTAIN; OR THE WAR OF ALL NATIONS (Ralph Bonehill / Edward Stratemeyer, 1902)

## Front matter
- Title page: "The Young Naval Captain; or The War of All Nations," by Captain Ralph Bonehill, Thompson & Thomas, Chicago, 1902.
- Preface: author's two aims: (1) naval/science progress; (2) US growth (13 states to many; flag from Maine to Luzon, Alaska to Texas and Porto Rico). Closing exhortation to boys: "the humble rail-splitter or the canal-boat boy can become President."
- Chapter list (30): I United States Against the World; II First Battle on the Ocean; III Interview with Secretary of Navy; IV Blowing Up of the Tien-Tsin; V Prisoners of the Sea; VI Out of a Living Tomb; VII Attack on Japanese Troops; VIII Act of a Madman; IX Another Blowing Up; X Fraudulent Message; XI Urgent Call for the Holland XI; XII Defeat Turned Into Victory; XIII Central American Canal; XIV Cast Upon the Shore; XV Tidal Waves and Whales; XVI Saving the Merchantman; XVII Playing the Spy; XVIII Capture of Hang Chang; XIX News of the President's Daughter; XX Cave Under the Ocean; XXI Out of One Danger Into Another; XXII A Run Not Wanted; XXIII Fight off Cape Nome; XXIV Sinking of the Ivan II; XXV Holland XI Captured; XXVI Prisoners on the Holland XI; XXVII Defeat of the Enemy; XXVIII Underwater Earthquake; XXIX Rescue of Jean Fevre; XXX Last Battle—Conclusion.

## Ch I (1936, spring)
- Andy Greggs (18, tall, blue eyes, curly brown hair; machinist at Standard Shipyard, Bridgeport) and Oscar Pelham (nearly 20, black eyes/hair) discuss "war against the world." Bonus $50,000 if three new warships floated by July 1 (six weeks).
- Background: US ~100M people; President Jefferson McKinley Adams (6 yrs in office); army 500,000; navy 500 warships. US includes all North America Isthmus of Panama to Hudson Bay, West Indies, Hawaii, Philippines, parts of China/Japan. Cuba a state; Canada broke from England; Yellow War of 1925 (China); South Africa Boers freed; Turkey debt, Turks defeated 1928.
- Oscar's father Commodore David Pelham (Civil & Spanish-American war vet, died; Oscar orphaned; wealth to Oscar). Oscar trained at Edison's Electrical University, Llewellyn Park. Worked at Standard Ship Yard.
- Holland X seen at Elizabethport; Oscar's Vermont-inventor boat anecdote (sank, blew up). George Dross = oldest engineer.
- Oscar's boat design: aluminum & steel, 115 ft long, 16 ft wide, 8–11.5 ft high, cigar-shaped, windows; twin electric screws; 23 knots; 20 days' air; torpedoes & dynamite bombs. Model named "Holland XI." Trial in Long Island Sound with Andy.

## Ch II
- War declared; foreign nations (England, France, Germany, Russia, Japan, etc.) against US. Cuba, Philippines admitted; Brazil, Chile, Peru, Honduras seeking admission. Mexico admitted; Aguinaldo dead.
- NY war march; balloons; Empire building 56 stories.
- Navy: Holland (1900) and Hollands III, V, VI, IX, X; II, IV, VII, VIII lost. Miles-Gilford rifles; Hotchkiss bomb guns at Sandy Hook.
- Gabretti (Italian naturalized engineer) blew up Holland I; reward $50,000.
- Foreign fleet ~15 ships off Nova Scotia; US 12 ships incl. armored cruiser Columbia (18,000 tons). Battle off Sandy Hook, rainy Saturday, 13 vs 12. Chicago sunk; German submarine sank three US cruisers; French sub sunk by Indiana's shells. Fleet retreated to NY.

## Ch III
- Oscar goes to Washington on Congressional Limited; Senator Forbish (NY) gives letter. Secretary of Navy Short sees Oscar; model (Holland X in corner). Oscar asks to command boat. Demonstration set for next day at 5 pm.

## Ch IV
- Test at government pond; President Adams present. Model works. Cost $200,000; Oscar asks more. Navy offers half a million if built in one month. Built in 29 days; launched NY bay.
- Crew of ten: Oscar captain; Andy first lieutenant; George Dross head engineer. Sails to Commodore Garrison (Cuba). Tien-Tsin (Chinese armored cruiser) bombards Baracoa. Torpedo with 5-min fuse blows up Tien-Tsin.
- French cruiser Republique fires dynamite shell at Holland.

## Ch V
- Oscar plays keyboard, Holland jerks away; Republique chases. Holland gets under keel; Cuban shore batteries (American old warships in bay) hit Republique; she sinks onto Holland, pinning her in sand. Torpedo fuse set 3 min fails (clockwork torn). Men: Marney (air man), Walton (ammunition man).

## Ch VI
- Air reservoir 215 feet = ~2 hours. Oscar goes out in diver suit via torpedo hole; keel of Republique splits and grips Holland. Blast from magazine knocks him out; Holland gone. Oscar climbs out, removes helmet near Cuba coast 2 miles west of Baracoa. Japanese troops (1,000+) find him at dawn.

## Ch VII
- Japanese officer keeps Oscar alive; diver suit taken. Japanese landing ~6,000 Chinese/Japanese at Baracoa; plan to march to Havana then Key West/Florida.
- Andy surfaces (Holland XI), rescues Oscar with knife; Andy's pistol kills Japanese soldier. Escape. Dynamite bombs fired from surfaced Holland into Japanese column: ~50 killed, Japanese commander beheaded; rest flee.

## Ch VIII
- Commodore Garrison (flagship) orders Holland to Canada to join Admiral Fielding. Sargasso Sea tangle; escape with dynamite bomb.
- Admiral Fielding at Gulf of St. Lawrence. Lieutenant Raxtell (pale, sent to watch) goes mad, prepares to blow up Holland in magazine; Oscar tackles; Walton helps; Raxtell bound & masked. (Later put ashore at Boston.)

## Ch IX
- Enemy fleet: 34 warships, 66 transports. Holland torpedoes Wilhelm II (German gunboat), Terrible (British cruiser), Philippe (French ship-of-line) — times set 30, 20, 10 min; blows at 11:30. Oscar prefers big guns; torpedo cost $8,600.
- Highite explosive (new): shell throws hundreds of small shells.

## Ch X
- Cape Cod harbor; Andy reports Martha Adams (President's daughter) kidnapped from White House; $100,000 reward. Oscar sweet on Martha (met three times at shipyard).
- Fake order to Cape Cod; copper netting trap with mine; Holland backs away. Lookout: English despatch boat; Holland rams it, sinks it. Messenger = lieutenant.

## Ch XI
- Oscar's suggestion: secret marking of real messages; three false messengers hanged as spies.
- Anchor from fishing smack wrecks screw; Holland towed to Charlestown Navy Yard for repair.
- Battle off Casco Bay (Portland): US vs allies (~28 vs 32); Berlin, Carlos II, Siene sunk; Utah & Tennessee burn; Windsor sunk by New Jersey; New York rams French ship. Oscar signal: "Have just finished repairs"; Admiral: "Come to Casco Bay instantly."

## Ch XII
- Holland sinks British armored cruiser (Iowa III saved), French Coronet (torpedo holes), German cruisers near Virginia (torpedo between them), highite bombs on enemy; Turkish ship, Italian corvette, transport (2,000 soldiers) destroyed. Victory.
- Repairs at Boston. Fleet of 50 Chinese/Japanese/Russian ships heads for San Francisco. Admiral Alvin Chester (Pacific) telegram: "You are wanted immediately on the pacific coast... Chester." Route via Central American Canal (completed, $36M).

## Ch XIII
- Canal: at Ambrose (Spanish town) message; Spaniards Carlos & Pargloss gossip. Nathan Pargloss (ex-Treasury, dismissed, $5,000/year) plotted lock sabotage; Oscar sets trap; Pargloss in boat with dynamite at lock; Oscar shoots him in shoulder; Pargloss drowns clinging to stump.

## Ch XIV
- Holland reaches San Francisco (ovation); heads to Honolulu (three hundred thousand people). Enemy captured Honolulu; Diamond Head flag.
- Oscar sets electric-wire mines on eight enemy ships; at 7:50 blow-up; eight foreign officers captured.
- Under-water earthquake; tidal wave 15 ft throws Holland 200 ft ashore onto rocks. Three more warships approaching.

## Ch XV
- Holland fires highite on Russian ship; Chinese & Japanese fire; second tidal wave; the three warships wrecked on rocks. Holland returns to Honolulu. Whale school; whale rams trap-door; Oscar shoves signal shell into whale's mouth, whale destroyed.

## Ch XVI
- Thunder storm kills a sailor (first death). Burial at sea with Bible reading.
- Merchantman (American, for Philippines) chased by two Japanese warships; Holland torpedoes one, frightens other. Over thirty foreign warships off Golden Gate; plotting; Oscar goes aboard British ship Corcoran in dark.

## Ch XVII
- Oscar in Corcoran (Captain Gresson, British; Chinese captains Hang Chang & Chan Lee?—second Chinese captain unnamed in text). Negro servant killed by Oscar's knife. Overheard plot: abduction of President's daughter used as ransom for China's demands; attack on SF at sunrise (7 ships); remainder (Russian admiral) to Alaska. Oscar posing as "Barton Peeks" (British spy). Chinese captain Hang Chang wants to inspect boat; Holland had gone.

## Ch XVIII
- Hang Chang taken aboard Holland; second captain's warning; secret number code ("Sixteen" = enemy here; "Nine" = go down). Hang Chang chained. Oscar given command of future submarine squadron (commodore rank) plan, three more boats.

## Ch XIX
- Hang Chang reveals Martha Adams on Chinese warship Green Dragon, sailed Chesapeake Bay south to Cuba coast, alone. Oscar threatens torture (bluff). Hang Chang's warships: Pekin and Shanghai.

## Ch XX
- Pekin destroyed at SF bombardment; Japanese warship sinks; Tokio anchor entangles Holland; Tokio blown up by torpedo at Fisherman's Bay after rescue of American transport (1,600 soldiers from Tacoma). Holland heads to Alaska; Cape Nome gold ($35M gold, $18M silver at bank).
- Ocean cave; trapped by landslide.

## Ch XXI
- Sea serpent (30 ft) killed by dynamite shell in mouth. Escape by blasting rock. Lightning strikes Holland; George Dross, Andy knocked out; electrical circuits wrecked; Holland runs wild; Oscar stops circling.

## Ch XXII
- Switchboard burnt out; Oscar fixes. Gilson (helper) assists. Oscar uses rubber gloves.

## Ch XXIII
- Holland stopped; repairs; duplicate switchboard. Russian cruiser Ivan II (largest; 100+ guns, 2,000 men) and fleet approach Cape Nome. Trap-door jam; Russians throw bomb; Oscar catches and hurls it up—shell explodes.

## Ch XXIV
- Russians set underwater alarm wires; Oscar floats torpedo on a line; blows hole in Ivan II; Ivan II sinks; 209 Russians captured including an Admiral. Hang Chang leaps overboard dragging Oscar.

## Ch XXV
- Andy rescues Oscar (knife, Hang Chang dies). Congress medal; Oscar rumored to be made commodore. Holland at Central American canal; machinery stops (repairs). Spanish captain Roquez & Italian/Spanish boarders capture Holland while Walton dozes; Marney & others subdued; Canelli sentry.

## Ch XXVI
- Roquez; Gabretti (ex-engineer, traitor, reward $50,000) runs engines; Dross tied. Oscar & Andy escape bonds using couch iron edge.

## Ch XXVII
- Oscar and Andy defeat Roquez (cut), Canelli killed by electric rifle; Gabretti kicked; Dross freed. Prisoners delivered to Santiago de Cuba garrison.

## Ch XXVIII
- Peace talks: foreign nations tired. Caribbean heat; undersea volcano & earthquake; Oscar's rescue attempt. Gromley Island, St. Pierre (30,000 dead) reference, NY downtown skyscraper.

## Ch XXIX
- Escape via port turn; Holland nearly thrown up. Wreck of French ship Bordeaux; survivor Jean Fevre (French dude; can't swim).

## Ch XXX (conclusion)
- Green Dragon at Cuban bay; Chinese officer (admiral) pursues Martha; Martha jumps overboard; Oscar shoots officer; Oscar rescues Martha; shot in shoulder. Andy torpedoes Green Dragon. War ends; US wins; Martha found; President Adams gives reward; Oscar commodore. Two years later Oscar Rear Admiral Pelham, married Martha; Andy commodore of one squadron, George Dross the other.

# BOOK 2 of 2: THE PILLAR OF LIGHT (Louis Tracy, 1904, Edward J. Clode, New York)

Epigraph: Matthew vii:25 ("the house that stood upon a rock"). Dedication/ TOC: Ch I Flotsam … XIX The House that Stood Upon a Rock.

## Ch I Flotsam (June, Gulf Rock lighthouse, Scilly Isles/Cornwall)
- Stephen Brand (~50, handsome, gentleman, once bitter re London/women, "two years ago fled London") is assistant-keeper; Jim Spence (lame from Egyptian campaign; Penzance; wife, three kids; cheerful sailor) assistant-keeper; Jones (head keeper, sciatica, Baptist, whitewash & polish type). Thompson the third assistant on leave.
- Morning; Princess Royal (liner, homeward Southampton) passes; derelict white ship's life-boat with broken mast; cormorants & birds. Brand swims out (Leander reference); shark (blue shark ~12 ft) attacks; Brand kills it with knife; dead man in boat thrown overboard; baby found under sail (girl, ~1 yr). Jim & Jones watch.

## Ch II A Christening
- Baby fed milk by handkerchief; named "E. T." laundry marks; gold brooch with four-leafed shamrock set in emeralds. Jones's wife Mrs. Jones; nurse Mrs. Sheppard (Brand's daughter's nurse). Brand says he'll adopt. Doctor from Penzance. Name chosen "Trevillion" (surname), Enid (first name, from Arthurian Enid).
- Constance Brand (Brand's daughter, ~8-ish at start; mother died when Constance was 13 months old; mother Madeleine Nanette de Courtray).

## Ch III The Signal (January, ~18 yrs later; Enid 19)
- Penzance; Ben Pollard (old fisherman) and pilchard-driver Daisy. Enid (flaxen, blue eyes, 19), Constance (brown hair, hazel eyes). Lt John Percival Stanhope (Jack; RN; mother Lady Margaret Stanhope; father Sir Charles; Tregarthen Lodge) meets them at quay; Jack's torpedo-boat ran aground at Portsea.
- Rocket signals ("Help wanted"); girls aboard Daisy go to Gulf Rock in snow; Brand signals Bates (broken leg) & Jackson (scalded). Girls hauled up in skip.

## Ch IV The Voice of the Reef
- Jackson & Bates sent ashore on Daisy; Jack in steam-yacht Lapwing (10 tons) comes; Lapwing can't land. Semaphore messages. Brand's auriscope (sound-direction instrument). Tide & gale. Barometer falling.

## Ch V The Hurricane
- Enid's memory; Brand explains auriscope; Lighthouse features (4,000 tons granite; 130 ft high; colza oil; eight-wick burner). Hurricane (No. 12 scale). Storm kills lantern vane; girls sent below for cocoa.

## Ch VI The Middle Watch
- Storm peak; Brand's joke; girls return. Steamer (Chinook, Atlantic liner, New York to Southampton, ex-Princess Royal rechristened) signals; rockets; Chinook wrecked on reef. Captain (Perkins) goes down with ship. Pyne (young American, Charles A. Pyne; Philadelphian; nephew of Cyrus J. Traill) climbs mast, rope to lighthouse.

## Ch VII The Lottery
- Chinook breaks in two. ~80 rescued via rope; Brand organizes; Pyne is last-but-one; captain lost. Enid & Constance serve.

## Ch VIII An Interlude
- Injured in hospital room; Mr. Emmett (chief officer, Chinook); Mrs. Vansittart (lady in lower bunk; collapses seeing Constance; asks "Who are you?"; "Constance Brand"; faints).
- Brand tells Emmett food for ~81 people for ~2 days; six-day minimum rations plan; oil (colza, 3,000 gallons) "a vegetable oil."

## Ch IX Mrs. Vansittart
- Passenger list: 37 crew, 33 saloon passengers (19 women), 7 steerage men & 1 woman. Pyne's uncle Cyrus J. Traill (Philadelphia millionaire) was to marry Mrs. Vansittart in Paris.
- Enid tells Mrs. Vansittart about her origin (E. T., adopted). Constance meets Mrs. Vansittart at stairs; Mrs. Vansittart asks to see Brand; Brand refuses (oil low, journal etc).

## Ch X Pyne's Progress
- Telegram: "Chinook... 78 survivors in lighthouse—captain, 201 passengers, officers and crew lost." Falcon (steam trawler, Stapleton). Pyne with Elsie & Mamie (little girls, Mrs. Taylor the nurse; mother drowned). Biscuit shared secretly; Brand's breakfast given to children; Brand's "Keep off" joke.

## Ch XI Mrs. Vansittart's Fear
- Rations: meat/potato; distilling water from canvas coil; food shortage; Pyne jokes; Mrs. Vansittart tells Traill has come on Falcon; Brand's signal to Mrs. Vansittart: "Mr. Cyrus J. Traill... sends his love to Etta and Charlie." She wants to leave Penzance at once; "I quitted New York yesterday week…"

## Ch XII Preparations
- Pyne & Brand agree: Brand will stand watch; sacrifice plan (Brand's secret to save daughters, 8 to 12 watch). Brand steals food (kitchen lockers). Trawler Falcon; Trinity tender; raft attempt fails.
- Brand's message to shore; Stanhope's signal "Mother sends her love to Enid."

## Ch XIII Before the Dawn
- Mr. Emmett falls ill; methylated spirit drunk by mutineers; rain collected. Pyne & Brand talk; Pyne says his parents lost at sea on yacht Esmeralda (age 6). Brand describes his "wife"? Brand thanks God for no heredity ("Thank God, yes!"). Mrs. Vansittart climbs stairs, tells Pyne she "thought she knew" Brand; cries.

## Ch XIV The Way They Have in the Navy
- Pyne & girls cooking; ham bone; store-room pilfering suspected. Stanhope decides to row boat to ladder; Brand dumps colza oil on sea (oil calms waves). Stanhope's boat with two rowers (Ben Pollard, Jim Spence) reaches; rope thrown; Stanhope hit in face; tug (Traill's hired) hauls. Enid looks out.

## Ch XV Enid's New Name
- Rope lines; supplies sent in watertight tins (water, milk, bread). Traill to Pyne: wrote to Brand. Traill's letter (dated) to Brand: Enid = his daughter Edith Traill; brooch & "E. T." identify her; Stanhope & Traill's engagement to Mrs. Vansittart; Mrs. Vansittart rejects Traill (letter: "I cannot marry you").

## Ch XVI Stephen Brand Explains
- Elsie & Mamie on stairs; children to tug; Traill meets Enid. Brand comes ashore; Mrs. Vansittart's face: Brand recognizes her — "When I knew her her name was Nanette... my wife." Constance: "Do you mean that she is my mother?"

## Ch XVII Mrs. Vansittart Goes Home
- Brand's story: Sir Stephen Brand, ninth baronet, of Lesser Hambledon, Northumberland; attaché at British Embassy Paris; married Nanette (Madeleine Nanette de Courtray, Jersey, 18 vs his 28); she had affair with a rich Frenchman; duel; he killed the Frenchman; she went to him, deserted; Mrs. Sheppard brought Constance to England. Traill: Edith (Enid) lost in boat in Esmeralda collision (July 21, Scilly/Fastnet fog); Esmeralda sank; Brand found boat July 30.
- Mrs. Vansittart at cottage door; faints; taken in.

## Ch XVIII Enid Wears an Old Ornament
- Lady Margaret & Jack; Traill's family: Esmeralda collision (Nova Scotian barque John S.); Mrs. Vansittart (Etta) "Nanette" former wife; Mr. Emmett confirms Enid resembles Traill's wife; Traill: Enid = Edith.

## Ch XIX The House That Stood Upon a Rock
- Week later: Mrs. Vansittart (Nanette) in cottage; Brand meets Nanette; she confesses divorce in Nebraska on grounds of desertion; she married Traill in Engadine; Brand forgives. Marriages: Pyne & Constance (Pyne to Italy; Constance now "Lady Brand"? wedding London); Stanhope & Enid (Riviera, Rome). Nanette & Brand remarry in Nebraska? (they sail west from Southampton to Far West). Last line: lighthouse "winking portentously... running away with your own wife."

---

NOTE: Names (Dross, Walton, Marney, Gilson, Chester, etc.) and sequences above are as stated in text.
